stem: The larger a group of adjacent 1s in a K-map, the fewer inputs its product term needs.

stem: The Quine-McCluskey method repeatedly applies which theorem?
explanation: Minterms differing in one bit combine and that bit drops out.
source: CSC 213 DLC course book.pdf (Digital Logic Design, Nancy C. Woods), Lecture Eight

stem: A half adder's carry output is produced by which gate?
explanation: The sum is the XOR of A and B; the carry is their AND.
source: CSC 213 DLC course book.pdf (Digital Logic Design, Nancy C. Woods), Lecture Nine

stem: A device that selects one of many inputs and passes it to a single output is a
explanation: The multiplexer is a data selector; the demultiplexer is a data distributor.
source: CSC 213 DLC course book.pdf (Digital Logic Design, Nancy C. Woods), Lecture Nine

stem: Which circuit is the odd one out?
explanation: The JK flip-flop is a sequential element; the others are combinational circuits.
source: CSC 213 DLC course book.pdf (Digital Logic Design, Nancy C. Woods), Lectures Nine and Ten

stem: When two inputs are active together, a priority encoder outputs the code of the highest-priority input.
explanation: A plain binary encoder would give a wrong code in that case.
source: CSC 213 DLC course book.pdf (Digital Logic Design, Nancy C. Woods), Lecture Nine
